title: Senior Staff Nurse (Band 6), Acute Medical Unit
company: Marrowby and Castlefold NHS Foundation Trust
description:
Senior Staff Nurse (Band 6), Acute Medical Unit

Marrowby and Castlefold NHS Foundation Trust
Castlefold General Hospital, Castlefold

Band 6: £37,338 to £44,962 a year, per annum, pro rata
Contract: Permanent
Working pattern: Full-time, 37.5 hours a week, flexible working, internal rotation of days and nights
Reference number: 999-AMU-1107-F
Closing date: 30 November 2026

Job summary

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic and motivated Senior Staff Nurse to join our busy 36-bed Acute Medical Unit (AMU) at Castlefold General Hospital. The unit admits up to 60 patients a day from the emergency department, GP referrals and our same day emergency care service, and supports them through the first 72 hours of their stay.

You will be an experienced Band 5 nurse ready for the next step. As a Band 6 you will lead a team of registered nurses and healthcare support workers on each shift, coordinate the unit in the absence of the nurse in charge, and act as a role model for safe, compassionate care. You will support the Ward Manager and Band 7 Sisters and Charge Nurses with the day-to-day running of the unit, including bed management, staffing and the flow of patients to specialty wards.

We are proud of our teaching culture. You will supervise and assess pre-registration nursing students, support newly qualified nurses through their preceptorship, and help us develop the next generation of acute medical nurses.

Main duties of the job

- Assess, plan, deliver and evaluate evidence-based care for acutely unwell adult patients, many of whom are frail or have complex needs.
- Take charge of the unit when required, allocating staff and patients and coordinating admissions, discharges and transfers with the site team.
- Recognise and respond to the deteriorating patient, escalating promptly using NEWS2 and the trust's sepsis pathway.
- Triage and prioritise new admissions from the emergency department and the same day emergency care service.
- Administer intravenous medicines and fluids, cannulate and take blood in line with trust competencies.
- Act as a practice supervisor and practice assessor for nursing students and support the preceptorship of newly qualified staff.
- Lead and take part in clinical audit and quality improvement projects on the unit.
- Report and learn from incidents through the trust's incident reporting system and take part in clinical governance meetings.
- Safeguard vulnerable adults and children, and apply the Mental Capacity Act in everyday practice.

About us

Marrowby and Castlefold NHS Foundation Trust provides acute and community services to around 520,000 people across Castlefold, Marrowby and the surrounding villages. We employ more than 7,000 staff across two hospitals and 14 community sites. Our values of kindness, respect and ambition guide everything we do, and we are committed to being an inclusive employer where every member of staff can thrive.

We offer a generous benefits package, including NHS Pension, 27 days' annual leave rising with service, a salary sacrifice cycle and car scheme, on-site nursery places, staff health and wellbeing services, and access to our education centre and library.

Detailed job description and main responsibilities

Clinical practice

The postholder will be accountable for their own practice and will deliver high standards of nursing care in line with the NMC Code. They will carry out holistic assessments on admission, including falls, pressure ulcer, nutrition and delirium screening, and will use these to plan care with patients and their families.

They will be competent in intravenous therapy, peripheral cannulation and venepuncture, and will be expected to develop skills in arterial blood gas sampling and the care of patients receiving non-invasive ventilation, with training provided by the unit's practice educator.

They will recognise early signs of deterioration, record and act on NEWS2 observations, and escalate to the medical team and the critical care outreach team without delay. They will be confident in responding to cardiac arrest and medical emergencies and will hold, or be willing to work towards, Advanced Life Support certification.

Leadership and management

The postholder will take charge of the unit on a regular basis, including at night. This includes allocating patients and staff according to skill mix and acuity, coordinating admissions and discharges with the site manager, and making sure that the unit is safe at handover.

They will manage staff concerns and complaints at a local level and escalate to the Ward Manager where needed. They will contribute to the recruitment, induction and appraisal of Band 5 nurses and healthcare support workers.

They will make sure that equipment, controlled drugs and stock are checked and that the unit's environment is safe and clean.

Education and training

The postholder will act as a practice supervisor and practice assessor in line with the NMC Standards for student supervision and assessment. They will support newly qualified nurses through the trust's preceptorship programme and teach junior staff at the bedside and in the unit's teaching sessions.

They will take responsibility for their own continuing professional development, maintain their NMC revalidation, and keep their mandatory training up to date.

Quality and governance

The postholder will take part in clinical audit, including the monthly nursing care indicators, and will lead at least one quality improvement project a year. They will report incidents promptly, take part in investigations and share the learning with the team. They will understand and apply the principles of clinical governance, infection prevention and control, and information governance.

Safeguarding

The postholder will follow the trust's safeguarding adults and children procedures, recognise and report concerns, and apply the Mental Capacity Act 2005 and Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards when assessing patients' capacity to make decisions about their care.

Communication

The postholder will communicate clearly and compassionately with patients, families and carers, including when giving difficult news. They will work closely with doctors, therapists, pharmacists, discharge coordinators and the wider multidisciplinary team, and will keep accurate, contemporaneous records in the electronic patient record.

Health and safety

The postholder must take reasonable care of their own health and safety and that of others who may be affected by their actions. They must follow the trust's health and safety policies, use the equipment and protective clothing provided, and report accidents, near misses and hazards straight away.

Infection prevention and control

All staff are responsible for protecting patients, visitors and colleagues from infection. The postholder will follow the trust's infection prevention and control policies, including hand hygiene, the use of personal protective equipment, the safe handling of sharps and the isolation of patients with known or suspected infections. They will act as a role model for junior staff and challenge poor practice.

Confidentiality and information governance

The postholder must keep all information about patients and staff confidential, in line with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and the Caldicott principles. They must only access records they need for their work, and must keep electronic and paper records secure at all times.

Equality, diversity and inclusion

The trust is committed to equality of opportunity for all staff and patients. The postholder will treat everyone with dignity and respect, and will challenge discrimination wherever they see it.

Working for our organisation

Our Acute Medical Unit opened in a new building in 2024 and has single rooms with en-suite facilities, a dedicated procedure room and a seminar room for teaching. The team includes acute physicians, advanced clinical practitioners, a practice educator, a discharge coordinator, physiotherapists and occupational therapists, and a ward pharmacist. Nurses on the unit rotate between the assessment area, the short-stay beds and the ambulatory service, so you will see a wide range of acute medical conditions, including sepsis, respiratory failure, diabetic emergencies and acute kidney injury.

We support flexible working and will consider requests for part-time hours, compressed hours and self-rostering. We offer a structured development programme for new Band 6 nurses, with protected study time and a named mentor in your first year.

This job description is not exhaustive and may be reviewed in discussion with the postholder.
